A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TF-TI2I study and provide readable text, equations, eight figures and three tables. Both end with references on page 11; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on FG-TI2I, DreamBench and Wild-TI2I, alongside contextual-token experiments and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, contextual-token experiments and ablations.

M1.justification: The SD3.5-large backbone, Contextual Tokens Sharing, Reference Contextual Masking and Winner Takes All procedures are retained. The abbreviated noise notation does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same FG-TI2I reference scenarios involving objects, textures, actions and backgrounds, plus DreamBench customization and Wild-TI2I editing. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3 and Figure 6. FG-TI2I retains MasaCtrl, StyleAlign, OmniGen and Emu2; the DreamBench and Wild-TI2I comparator rows also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 750 DreamBench instances, 148 Wild-TI2I instances and 100 generated prompts per FG-TI2I subtask. Section 5 removes CDS from the reference-alignment bullet, but retains it under prompt following and in Table 3; no evaluated metric or testing procedure changes.

E4.justification: The reference-subtraction examples, t-SNE analysis, token-replacement experiment and RCM/WTA ablations remain unchanged in Figures 1, 3, 4 and 8. Removing the unresolved pointer to additional results does not remove any supplied analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the same two-seed illustration in Section 4.1. Neither adds benchmark repeated-run information, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 match, and the qualitative result images are unchanged. For example, TF-TI2I retains DreamBench scores of 33.1 and 79.1, and Wild-TI2I scores of 30.4 and 0.115.

T1.justification: Equation (5) and Section 4.3 shorten ε(τ_I^0, t) to ε(t), retaining the same Gaussian-or-inversion noise description. This is a notation simplification without a stated new assumption or derivation; the substantive attention and masking mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about implicit-context learning, training-free TI2I generation, RCM/WTA and FG-TI2I. The claim of leading on 12 of 18 FG-TI2I metrics is unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the semantic-fidelity versus low-level-detail tradeoff and the limitation caused by imprecise RCM segmentation. The deleted CTS sentence repeats the distribution-shift rationale retained in the introduction and ablation discussion.

D1.justification: The disclosed backbone configuration, Otsu masking, ChatGPT-4o prompt generation, Flux 1.0 dev reference generation and project-page link remain unchanged. No implementation, resource or access information is substantively added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 64 references and research positioning are retained. Section 2.2 expands KNN-D to KNN-Diffusion while citing the same work, reference 48.

P1.justification: v2 removes two unresolved '??' cross-reference passages, corrects 'implcit-context', expands the KNN-Diffusion name and adds funding acknowledgments. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 changes its CLIP-Text header from CP-T to CP. Equation spacing and pagination shift, Figure 8 moves within page 8, and printed page numbers disappear. The same figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves editorial clarity by removing unresolved cross-references, including a pointer to additional results absent from the supplied PDF, and making Table 2's metric label consistent with Section 5. The scientific evidence, reproducibility information and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
